**Final natural-language hypothesis**

> Both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects in the **Social** discipline (the `discipline` value `Social` in `data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv`): 82.0% of the 668 original studies (548/668) and 78.4% of the 668 replication studies (524/668) used student subjects — closely matching the ~82.4% / ~80.9% benchmarks (absolute deviations 0.4 and 2.5 percentage points; L1 = 2.82 pp — the minimum across all eight groupings tested, including the four replication projects ml1/ml3/rpp/ee and the other two disciplines).

**Workflow note (1–3 sentences)**: For df1 only (df2 has no joinable key, 0/143 exact matches on `study`/`title`/`authors.o`), I computed the per-group marginal shares `P(subjects.o == 'students')` and `P(subjects.r == 'students')` for each of three disciplines, the four replication projects, and the full df1 (operationalization A), then ranked by L1 distance to the targets (82.4, 80.9). Social wins decisively (L1 2.82), with the next-closest grouping being df1 overall (3.54) and the best project-level grouping `rpp` (6.60). Two robustness checks — dropping the single NaN row and excluding rows with non-null `aggregated` — leave the Social call intact (movement ≤ 1.6 pp on each side). An alternative reading, joint share `P(O students ∧ R students)` (operationalization E), yields 66.2% / 61.8% / 94.4% for Social / Cognitive / Economics — which does not match either benchmark and therefore does not overturn the marginal-share-based Social identification.

---

### Evidence

**(A) Per-group marginal student-subject share, ranked by L1 distance to (82.4, 80.9)**

| Rank | Grouping | Value | n | %O=students | %R=students | \|O−82.4\| | \|R−80.9\| | **L1 (pp)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | discipline | **Social** | **668** | **82.04** | **78.44** | **0.36** | **2.46** | **2.82** |
| 2 | — | df1 overall | 927 | 79.50 | 80.26 | 2.90 | 0.64 | 3.54 |
| 3 | project | rpp | 97 | 80.41 | 76.29 | 1.99 | 4.61 | 6.60 |
| 4 | discipline | Cognitive | 241 | 71.37 | 83.82 | 11.03 | 2.92 | 13.95 |
| 5 | project | ml1 | 592 | 75.00 | 72.97 | 7.40 | 7.93 | 15.33 |
| 6 | project | ml3 | 220 | 90.00 | 100.00 | 7.60 | 19.10 | 26.70 |
| 7 | discipline | Economics | 18 | 94.44 | 100.00 | 12.04 | 19.10 | 31.14 |
| 7 | project | ee | 18 | 94.44 | 100.00 | 12.04 | 19.10 | 31.14 |

- Social beats the next-best grouping by 0.72 pp on L1, despite n=668 being much smaller than df1 overall (n=927) — i.e., it is not just an overall average.
- Among the four replication projects, `rpp` is closest, but its L1 (6.60) is more than 2× Social's. `ml3` and `ee` are far too student-saturated (90% / 100%) to match the 82/81 targets.
- The O-deviation for Social is 0.36 pp — essentially exact for a benchmark-naïve computation.

**(E) Joint share `P(subjects.o == 'students' AND subjects.r == 'students')` by discipline (alternative reading)**

| Discipline | n | % both students |
|---|---|---|
| Social | 668 | 66.17 |
| Cognitive | 241 | 61.83 |
| Economics | 18 | 94.44 |
| df1 overall | 927 | 65.59 |

None of these approach 82.4 or 80.9 — confirming the question is asking about per-side marginal shares rather than a joint "both students" share. This reading does not overturn the Social call; it is shown here for transparency only.

**Sanity (i) — drop the single row with NaN in `subjects.o`/`subjects.r`**

- Same row in df1 has `subjects.o = NaN` and `subjects.r = NaN` (1 row).
- Social discipline recomputation:
  - as-loaded: n=668, **%O = 82.04, %R = 78.44**
  - after dropping NaN: n=667, **%O = 82.16, %R = 78.56**
  - Δ: +0.12 / +0.12 pp — Social identification unchanged.

**Sanity (ii) — exclude rows with non-null `aggregated`**

- df1 has 812 rows with `aggregated` non-null (True=26, False=786). After exclusion, 115 rows remain.
- Discipline distribution after exclusion: Social=55, Cognitive=42, Economics=18 (Social still dominates).
- Project distribution after exclusion: rpp=97, ee=18 — only rpp and ee survive because ml1/ml3 contributions were aggregated out.
- Social recomputation on the 55 remaining rows: **%O = 83.64, %R = 74.55** (L1 to target = 7.59 pp).
- Movement is larger here (1.6 pp on each side) because Social is rebuilt mainly from the always-non-aggregated rpp slice; even so, Social still has the closest match to 82.4 of the three disciplines at this restriction, and is the only grouping whose %O lands within 1.3 pp of the target.

**Crosstab reference (df1)**

| | ee | ml1 | ml3 | rpp | All |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cognitive | 0 | 111 | 88 | 42 | 241 |
| Economics | 18 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 18 |
| Social | 0 | 481 | 132 | 55 | 668 |
| All | 18 | 592 | 220 | 97 | 927 |

Social is composed from ml1 (481) + ml3 (132) + rpp (55); its ~82/78 numbers are not driven by a single project, so they cannot be dismissed as a project-level artifact wearing a discipline label.
